title: Derived categories of etale sheaves
statement:
For a scheme $T$ let $T_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and for a commutative ring $R$ let $R_T$ be the constant sheaf of rings on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and
$\Mod(T_{\Et},R)=\Mod(R_T)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Define

$$
 D(T_{\Et},R)=D(\Mod(T_{\Et},R))
$$

to be its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: the localization of the category of cochain complexes of $R_T$-module sheaves at the quasi-isomorphisms, with its triangulated structure. The notation without $R$, $D(T_{\Et})$, means $D(\Ab(T_{\Et}))$ for the category $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ of sheaves of abelian groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] (the case $R=\mathbf Z$). For $K\in D(T_{\Et},R)$ and $i\in\mathbf Z$ write $\mathcal H^i(K)\in\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ for its $i$-th cohomology sheaf [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], the cohomology $\Ker d^i/\Im d^{i-1}$ of any representing complex.
Let

$$
 \Dplus(T_{\Et},R)=D^+(\Mod(T_{\Et},R)),\qquad D^b(T_{\Et},R)=D^b(\Mod(T_{\Et},R))
$$

be the bounded below and bounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]: the strictly full triangulated subcategories of $D(T_{\Et},R)$ of the $K$ for which there is an integer $n$ with $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for all $i<n$ (equivalently $K\in D(T_{\Et},R)^{\ge n}$ for the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]), respectively for which $\mathcal H^i(K)\neq0$ for only finitely many $i$. An object $K$ has *torsion cohomology* if every $\mathcal H^i(K)$, as a sheaf of abelian groups, is a torsion sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves].

split_report.summary: Rewrote the statement to introduce D(T_et,R) as D(Mod(R_T)) for the constant sheaf of rings R_T on the small etale site, H^i as the cohomology functors of the derived category, and D^+ and D^b precisely as the full triangulated subcategories of Stacks 05RU (H^i = 0 for i << 0, resp. for |i| >> 0; equivalently the union of the D^{>=n} of the standard t-structure, resp. D^+ cap D^-), replacing 'Verdier localization of the abelian category of complexes', which mixed the localization at quasi-isomorphisms with the Verdier quotient of K(A). Named every notion as a statement dependency: etale site, constant sheaf, sheaves of modules, etale sheaves (Ab, Mod(T_et,R), torsion), abstract derived category, cohomology sheaves, standard t-structure, and a new Mathlib leaf def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories (DerivedCategory.Plus/Minus/Bounded). Removed def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks, which the statement does not use. The D, D^+, D^b, H^i parts specialize in one line each from Mathlib (DerivedCategory/Plus/Bounded/homologyFunctor of SheafOfModules over constantSheaf on Scheme.smallEtaleTopology), but the item as a whole is not a one-line specialization: Mathlib has no torsion sheaf, so 'torsion cohomology' rests on the unsplit def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves.

lean.note: Mixed record (fixed by R-ddc1147 to the six-functor encoding of STATE 'Λ-MODULE ÉTALE SHEAVES: TWO ENCODINGS', the encoding of every landed proper-base-change citer). Existing: D(T_et,Λ) = AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.DerivedCategoryModule Λ T := DerivedCategory (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u+1} Λ)) (source WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Etale.Derived.Coefficients, Λ : Type (u+1), global HasDerivedCategory.ofIsGrothendieckAbelian); D(T_et) = DerivedCategory (Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u+1}) as in HasTorsionEtaleCohomology of def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves; H^i = DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i; D^+, D^b = DerivedCategory.Plus / DerivedCategory.Bounded of Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u+1} Λ) (Mathlib, def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories). New: torsionCohomology on all of D(T_et,Λ), every H^r(K) torsion as an abelian sheaf (CategoryTheory.Sheaf.IsTorsion after forget₂); on D^+ it is the source's Etale.DerivedCategory.Plus.torsionHomology via Scheme.isTorsionSheaf_iff_isTorsion. The delivered SheafOfModules encoding (independent coefficient universe v, four sheafification/smallness abbrevs, HasDerivedCategory.standard) is dropped.
